name: White Oak Desk Top
subtitle: Layered oak surface with a solid profiled perimeter
description: A parametric desk top built around a stable core, with either a continuous 1/8 in white-oak plywood veneer field or staggered unfinished white-oak flooring strips, plus a 1–2 in solid white-oak edge band that carries the corner radius, roundovers, and underside bevel.

dimensionTargets: The default desk top is 72 in long by 30 in deep with a 1 in stable core and a 1/8 in white-oak surface layer.
The surface can switch between one continuous white-oak plywood veneer field and staggered unfinished white-oak flooring strips.
A 1 1/2 in solid white-oak perimeter band surrounds the surface field and remains editable from 1 to 2 in.
The default perimeter uses a 1 in plan-view corner radius, a 1/4 in top roundover, a 1/8 in bottom roundover, and a 3/4 in underside bevel inset rising 5/8 in.
The flooring layout defaults to nominal 3 in faces with deterministic variable lengths from 18 to 48 in.
invariants: Keep overall length and depth independent from the model scale denominator.
Keep the stable core and selected white-oak surface field inside the solid perimeter band.
Keep the plan-view corner radius inside the solid band so the inset field never requires an unsupported curved corner patch.
Keep all routed roundovers and bevels inside solid edge-band stock with at least 1/4 in of uncut band remaining.
Keep the surface thickness independent so 1/8 in veneer plywood and thicker unfinished flooring stock can both be represented.
Keep flooring seams staggered and variable in length while preserving the exact inset-field envelope.
Treat the seam reveal as a modeling and layout aid; confirm actual tongue, groove, adhesive, movement, and substrate details from the selected flooring product.
Treat this as a fabrication model, not structural certification of the desk base, attachment method, or concentrated-load capacity.

scripts.name: audit
scripts.description: Validates the layered build, 1–2 in solid band, edge-profile stock, flooring layout range, and reference STL.
